title: Idempotent lifting for the structure sheaf over a henselian pair
statement:
Let $(A,I)$ be a henselian pair [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology], $S=\operatorname{Spec}A$, $S_0=\operatorname{Spec}(A/I)$, let $Z\to S$ be proper [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], and let $Z_0=Z\times_SS_0$ with its projection $i:Z_0\to Z$. Then:

(a) $W\mapsto W_0=W\times_SS_0=i^{-1}(W)$ is a bijection from the set of open and closed subsets of $Z$ to the set of open and closed subsets of $Z_0$. In particular an open and closed subset $W\subseteq Z$ with $W\times_SS_0=\emptyset$ is empty.

(b) Restriction $i^\sharp:H^0(Z,\mathcal O_Z)\to H^0(Z_0,\mathcal O_{Z_0})$ induces a bijection between the idempotents of the two rings: every idempotent of $H^0(Z_0,\mathcal O_{Z_0})$ lifts uniquely to an idempotent of $H^0(Z,\mathcal O_Z)$.

(The map $i^\sharp$ itself need not be bijective: for $A=k[[t]]$, $I=(t)$, $Z=\mathbf P^1_A$ it is $k[[t]]\to k$.)

proof.text: Restrict clopen subsets to the closed fibre using lem-weil-pbc-henselian-clopen-restriction, the first three steps of the previous proof. This supplies injectivity and a clopen lift of each closed-fibre clopen.

*Step 4 (statement (b)).* By [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-clopen-idempotent] (b), $e\mapsto U_e$ is a bijection from the idempotents of $H^0(Z,\mathcal O_Z)$ to the open and closed subsets of $Z$, and likewise for $Z_0$; by (c) of that lemma applied to $g=i$, $i^\sharp(e)$ is idempotent and $U_{i^\sharp(e)}=i^{-1}(U_e)$. So the map $e\mapsto i^\sharp(e)$ on idempotents is, through these two bijections, the map $W\mapsto i^{-1}(W)$ of Step 3, which is bijective. Hence $i^\sharp$ is bijective on idempotents: every idempotent of $H^0(Z_0,\mathcal O_{Z_0})$ is $i^\sharp(e)$ for exactly one idempotent $e$ of $H^0(Z,\mathcal O_Z)$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma 10.21.3 (Tag 00EE) for the correspondence on affine pieces; the passage to idempotents written out by the agent

proof.text: For injectivity, equal restricted idempotents have equal clopen loci on Y₀. Pullback compatibility identifies these with inverse images of their loci on Y, so clopen injectivity gives equal loci, and scheme_clopen_idempotent gives equal idempotents. For surjectivity, lift the locus of a closed-fibre idempotent to a clopen U on Y, realize U by an idempotent e, and use pullback compatibility and injectivity of the closed-fibre locus map to identify the restriction of e with the given idempotent.

blueprint_update.statement:
Let $(A,I)$ be a henselian pair [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology] and let
$Z\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ be proper [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions],
with closed fibre $Z_0=Z\times_AA/I$. Then every idempotent of
$H^0(Z_0,\mathcal O_{Z_0})$ lifts uniquely to an idempotent of $H^0(Z,\mathcal
O_Z)$; equivalently, restriction induces a bijection on idempotents, and the
open and closed subschemes of $Z_0$ are exactly the closed fibres of the open
and closed subschemes of $Z$.

proof.text:
The closed fibre $i:Z_0\to Z$ is a closed immersion whose image is
$p^{-1}(V(I))$, where $p:Z\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ is the structure map. By
[lemma-weil-pbc-stein-connectedness], $Z$ is spectral and every irreducible
closed subset of $Z$ meets $Z_0$ in a nonempty connected subset. In particular
every nonempty closed subset $C\subseteq Z$ meets $Z_0$: it contains the
closure of one of its points, which is irreducible.

*Open and closed subsets.* Let $U,V\subseteq Z$ be open and closed with
$U\cap Z_0=V\cap Z_0$. Then $U\setminus V$ is closed and does not meet $Z_0$,
so it is empty; likewise $V\setminus U$, hence $U=V$. Conversely let
$Z_0=V_1\sqcup V_2$ be a decomposition into open and closed subsets; each
$V_k$ is closed in $Z$, hence quasi-compact. Put
$W_k=\{x\in Z:\overline{\{x\}}\cap V_k\neq\emptyset\}$, the set of
generizations of $V_k$. Every $\overline{\{x\}}\cap Z_0$ is nonempty and
connected, so it lies in exactly one of $V_1,V_2$; hence $Z=W_1\sqcup W_2$ and
$W_k\cap Z_0=V_k$. Each $W_k$ is closed. Since $Z$ is spectral and $V_k$ is
quasi-compact, $W_k$ is the intersection of the quasi-compact opens containing
$V_k$, so it is pro-constructible, and every point $x$ of its closure is a
specialization of some $x'\in W_k$. A point $z\in\overline{\{x\}}\cap Z_0$
then lies in $\overline{\{x'\}}\cap Z_0\subseteq V_k$, so $x\in W_k$. Hence
$W_1$ is open and closed in $Z$ with closed fibre $V_1$. Thus $U\mapsto U\cap Z_0$ is a bijection from
the open and closed subsets of $Z$ to those of $Z_0$.

*Idempotents.* On any scheme $X$, an idempotent $e\in H^0(X,\mathcal O_X)$
determines the open and closed subset of points where its germ is $1$, and this
is a bijection between idempotents of $H^0(X,\mathcal O_X)$ and open and
closed subsets of $X$ [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]; it is compatible with
pullback along morphisms of schemes. Applied to $Z$ and $Z_0$ and the
restriction along $i$, the bijection on open and closed subsets becomes the
bijection on idempotents.

The restriction map $H^0(Z,\mathcal O_Z)\to H^0(Z_0,\mathcal O_{Z_0})$ itself
is not an isomorphism. For $A=k[[t]]$, $I=(t)$ and $Z=\mathbf P^1_A$ it is
$k[[t]]\to k$. So only idempotents are compared.
